name: Component Kit
description: A valuable upgrade material used to improve interactive parts and crafting stations in Survival.
imageAlt: component kit image from Scrap Mechanic

facts.label: Planning rule
facts.value: Upgrade around the next build goal

sections.heading: Spend for a Purpose
paragraphs: Component Kits are easiest to waste when every available upgrade looks useful. Decide what the next vehicle, farm, or production step needs, then spend only on the parts that remove that bottleneck.

sections.heading: Good Priorities
bullets: Unlock the production capacity required by the next confirmed recipe.
Improve a critical engine, seat, Controller, or other part only when the build needs it.
Keep a reserve for repairs and an unexpected progression requirement.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Component Kit - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Plan Component Kit spending for upgrades, crafting stations, vehicles, and Survival progression in Scrap Mechanic. Review its role before committing materials.

name: Scrap Metal
description: An early Survival material recovered from defeated Haybots and refined for basic construction.
imageAlt: scrap metal image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Early Metal Route
paragraphs: Haybots leave scrap that can be refined into useful early material. A short route through nearby ruins can support the first vehicle, but fighting several bots at once is riskier than returning for a second trip.

sections.heading: Collect Without Losing the Run
bullets: Listen before entering a ruin and pull one bot into open space.
Refine only when the area is safe.
Bring recovered material home before exploring farther.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Scrap Metal - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Find and manage Scrap Metal for early vehicles, construction, and Survival progression in Scrap Mechanic. Compare the practical requirements in-game.

name: Wood
description: A core building resource gathered from trees and processed into practical construction material.

sections.heading: Collection Is a Vehicle Problem
paragraphs: A good wood run keeps cutting equipment, loose resource objects, refinement, and cargo from interfering with one another. Start with a compact collector before building a huge forestry machine.
bullets: Clear the fall direction before cutting near the vehicle.
Keep the driver protected from moving logs.
Unload before the extra mass ruins steering.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Wood Gathering - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Gather, transport, refine, and store Wood efficiently for Scrap Mechanic building projects. Check its connected uses before the next Survival run.

name: Stone
description: A heavy raw resource gathered from rock formations and refined for construction and crafting.

sections.heading: Stability Comes Before Throughput
paragraphs: Stone collection puts uneven loads and impacts into a vehicle. A slow machine with a wide stance and protected controls usually completes more trips than a powerful drill mounted on a narrow chassis.
bullets: Lower the tool into the rock instead of driving the whole vehicle into it.
Separate collection from refinement if the first design becomes unstable.
Test the return route under full load.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Stone Mining - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Mine and transport Stone with a stable vehicle, controlled tool head, and safe return route in Scrap Mechanic. Check the related systems first.

name: Metal
description: A fundamental refined resource for stronger blocks, interactive parts, tools, and durable machines.

facts.label: Planning rule
facts.value: Reserve it for the proven design

sections.heading: Prototype Before Spending
paragraphs: Metal becomes expensive when every failed frame is built at final strength. Validate size and movement with cheaper material, then rebuild the load-bearing sections that need durability.
bullets: Keep a reserve for bearings, engines, and repairs.
Do not convert every resource before checking current recipes.
Store refined Metal separately from Scrap Metal.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Metal Resource - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Manage refined Metal for durable parts, stronger blocks, repairs, and efficient Scrap Mechanic construction. Check the related systems first.

name: Chemicals
description: A fluid crafting resource collected for material production and recipes that use chemical components.

sections.heading: Collect for a Recipe Plan
paragraphs: Chemical collection is easier to manage when the destination is known. Check the intended recipes, size the container for that batch, and avoid leaving an experimental collection machine loaded indefinitely.
bullets: Build a stable shoreline approach.
Keep collection controls reachable from safe ground.
Label chemical storage away from water and fuel.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Chemicals - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Collect and store Chemicals safely for planned crafting batches and material production in Scrap Mechanic. Compare the practical requirements in-game.

name: Oil
description: A collected Survival resource used in crafting chains connected to fuel and industrial production.

sections.heading: Separate Gathering from General Exploration
paragraphs: A dedicated collection trip carries the correct container and has space for the result. Mixing it with a long loot run often leaves the mechanic choosing between important cargo.
bullets: Check the current recipe requirement before leaving.
Use a vehicle that can recover from shoreline terrain.
Return with a useful batch instead of filling every slot.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Oil - Collection and Crafting Guide
seo.description: Plan Oil collection trips, storage, and fuel-related crafting in Scrap Mechanic Survival. Check its connected uses before the next Survival run.

name: Cotton
description: A harvestable natural resource used in crafting and garment-related progression.

sections.heading: Keep Natural and Farmed Supply Organized
paragraphs: Cotton can enter the base from exploration or farming. Store it near the recipes that consume it and avoid using every seed if the farm is meant to provide a repeatable supply.
bullets: Harvest natural Cotton when it fits the current route.
Keep planting stock separate from crafting stock.
Add a dedicated crop row only when demand is repeatable.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Cotton Resource - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Gather and organize Cotton from exploration or farming for Scrap Mechanic crafting and garment needs. Compare the practical requirements in-game.

name: Glue
description: A compact crafting resource made from Scrap Wood Block and Beeswax, required by many containers, tools, and utility parts.
imageAlt: Glue item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Treat Glue as a Shared Bottleneck
paragraphs: Glue appears across many unrelated recipes, so one planned machine can consume the reserve intended for another. Count finished Glue first, then multiply the wood and Beeswax cost before the gathering trip.

sections.heading: Stage Both Ingredients Together
bullets: One Glue needs 20 Scrap Wood Blocks and 2 Beeswax.
Keep Beeswax near the Craftbot instead of mixing it into general loot storage.
Use the generated list below to see exact current recipe quantities.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Glue Recipe and Crafting Uses
seo.description: Check the Scrap Mechanic Glue recipe, Scrap Wood Block and Beeswax cost, current properties, and every part that consumes Glue in Survival mode.

name: Pigment Flower
description: A harvestable color resource used by paint production, crafting recipes, and the Beeswax supply chain.
imageAlt: Pigment Flower item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Do Not Confuse Gathering with Crafting
paragraphs: The checked recipe data contains no finished-output Craftbot recipe for Pigment Flower. Build its supply around harvesting and renewable production, then reserve separate amounts for paint and for materials downstream of the flower.

sections.heading: Split the Harvest by Destination
bullets: Keep planting or production stock separate from immediate crafting stock.
Route a stable surplus toward the Beehive and Beeswax chain.
Check Paint Ammo and machine recipes before consuming the last stack.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Pigment Flower Uses and Supply
seo.description: Plan Pigment Flower gathering and production for Scrap Mechanic paint, Beeswax, and the current recipes that consume this resource in Survival.

name: Beeswax
description: A gathered and renewable workshop resource best known as the second ingredient in the Glue recipe.
imageAlt: Beeswax item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Gather for the Glue Total
paragraphs: Beeswax demand is easier to understand after converting the build plan into Glue. Every finished Glue requires two Beeswax, so a ten-Glue workshop project needs twenty before any other Beeswax recipe is counted.

sections.heading: Move from Scavenging to Production
bullets: Use gathered Beeswax for the first critical Glue crafts.
Develop the Pigment Flower and Beehive route when demand becomes repeatable.
Store the result beside Scrap Wood Block to make missing inputs obvious.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Beeswax for Glue and Crafting
seo.description: Calculate Scrap Mechanic Beeswax needs for Glue, compare its supply routes, and see the current recipes that consume it before the next workshop build.

name: Ember
description: A heat-related crafting resource first recovered from burned trees and then used in metal, glass, and workshop recipes.
imageAlt: Ember item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Keep One Ember to Grow the Supply
paragraphs: The checked Craftbot recipe consumes one Ember with fifty Scrap Wood Blocks and returns five. That means the batch adds four Ember, but it cannot start from zero; keep a seed unit instead of spending the last one on Glass or Metal Block upgrades.

sections.heading: Count the Whole Upgrade Chain
bullets: Metal Block Level 2 and Level 3 both add Ember costs.
Glass Block consumes one Ember per ten-block batch.
Stage Ember beside Water before starting a full Metal Block Level 3 run.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Ember Recipe, Sources and Uses
seo.description: Learn how Scrap Mechanic Ember supply grows from burned-tree Ember and Scrap Wood, then calculate Metal Block and Glass recipe costs for Survival crafting.

name: Glow
description: A luminous crafting resource produced through the Glowb feeding loop and consumed by lights and other glowing parts.
imageAlt: Glow item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Build a Supply Loop, Not a Recipe Queue
paragraphs: Glow is not listed as a direct Craftbot output in the checked data. Its practical route runs through a Glowb that consumes Cardboard, so the real inputs are creature access, feed stock, and collection time.

sections.heading: Reserve It for Finished Parts
bullets: Keep Cardboard Block production separate from structural Cardboard use.
Collect Glow in batches before beginning a multi-light build.
Use the generated recipe list to verify every current Glow quantity.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Glow and Glowb Production Guide
seo.description: Set up the Scrap Mechanic Glowb and Cardboard supply route for Glow, then review every current recipe that consumes the luminous resource safely.

name: Quartz
description: A mining-progression material used by advanced industrial machines and selected late-workshop recipes.
imageAlt: Quartz item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Quartz Belongs to the Mining Plan
paragraphs: Quartz is an input rather than a finished Craftbot output in the checked recipe set. Treat it as part of the Mining Hub and industrial-machine progression, and confirm the full machine bill before spending a partial stack.

sections.heading: Protect the Advanced-Machine Reserve
bullets: Store Quartz with other industrial materials instead of general Glass stock.
Check Component Kit and Metal Block requirements at the same time.
Use the recipe matches below as the version-specific quantity reference.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Quartz Mining Uses and Recipes
seo.description: Review Scrap Mechanic Quartz as a mining material and check its current advanced-machine recipes, quantities, and related workshop requirements.
